clue.text: Stand on the breakfast table

parts.note: reads like a person standing on the table, but means a rack that holds slices of grilled bread at breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a verb about someone climbing on the table; it is a noun, a holder sitting on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder for crisp grilled slices is a classic piece of breakfast tableware.

clue.text: Criminal's expenditure almost entirely on wife

indicators.note: almost entirely means the word is used with its final letter cut off

parts.note: an outlay is money spent, an expenditure

explanation.surface: A crook's spending goes nearly all on his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' drops the last letter Y of OUTLAY, leaving OUTLA; W follows it, 'on' meaning after in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw is a lawbreaker, someone living outside the protection of the law.

clue.text: Writer who makes his mark

parts.note: a writer here is anyone putting their name on a document, a mark being a signature or cross

explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author making a name for himself; really it is someone who just writes their name.
explanation.definitionFit: One who puts a signature on a contract literally makes a mark on the page.

clue.text: Gambling centre attracting Irish painter

parts.note: Reno in Nevada is a famous casino city

explanation.surface: A casino town draws an artist from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist artist.

clue.text: A motion picture's transformed on account of digital processing

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of the preceding words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A film is reworked for the digital age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges all fifteen letters of A MOTION PICTURES; 'on account of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a task onto computers is handling it by digital means.

clue.text: As a bossy official, I get a rule re-enacted

indicators.note: re-enacted means the letters of the words before it are acted out again in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A self-important official boasts of getting a regulation passed again.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-enacted' rearranges I GET A RULE; 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nazi district governor, the word now used for any domineering petty official.

clue.text: Came to a deal with pub and profited

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to have profited is to have gained

explanation.surface: Someone struck a deal in the pub and came out ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To have haggled is to have negotiated terms until reaching agreement.

clue.text: A stiff-faced cast

parts.note: stiff is slang for a corpse, and the cast is a plaster mould taken of its face

explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff-faced' suggests a stony expression or a wooden set of actors; a stiff is a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaster or wax mould taken from a dead person's features.

clue.text: Lady collecting silver — what's amount spent?

indicators.note: collecting means the lady takes the other piece inside her

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A woman gathering silver asks how much it cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the informal 'What's the damage?', meaning 'How much do I owe?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, the cost of something, as in asking the bill's total.

clue.text: Label for the ham maybe?

parts.note: the ham is an overacting actor, not meat, and the label is the professional name the actor works under

explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' suggests a sticker on a joint of meat; it is a poor actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's professional pseudonym, used in the theatre in place of a real name.

clue.text: Disease making naval captain tense

parts.note: William Bligh was captain of HMS Bounty, of the famous mutiny
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An illness that makes a ship's commander edgy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant disease, such as the one that ruined Irish potato crops.

clue.text: View admissions of debt as flippant

parts.note: a facet is an aspect, one view of something
IOUs (I owe you) are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: Someone regards owning up to debts as frivolous.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetious means joking at the wrong moment, treating serious things lightly.

clue.text: Sheep on motorway — into it goes one woman

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the sheep comes after the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written MI

indicators.note: into it goes means the next piece is put inside what has been built so far

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A sheep wanders onto the motorway and a woman drives into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a London-to-Yorkshire motorway, its 1 read as I; RAM after MI gives MIRAM, and 'into it goes' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, borne by Moses' sister in the Bible.

clue.text: Fifty-one, with competence, becoming a nuisance!

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals
ability is competence or skill

explanation.surface: A fifty-one-year-old, though capable, becomes a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or handicap, someone who causes more trouble than help.

clue.text: Sensational people running the company? Right!

parts.note: star as an adjective means outstanding or sensational
the board of directors runs a company

explanation.surface: Brilliant executives in charge of the firm win approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right!' looks like an exclamation of agreement; it means the right side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a vessel, the right-hand side when facing forward.

clue.text: Help to get mad Monica inside compound

indicators.note: inside means the scrambled name is placed within the word for help

parts.note: aid is help

indicators.note: mad means the letters of the name go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting help for Monica, who has gone mad, inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges MONICA to MINOAC, which 'inside' places within AID.
explanation.definitionFit: The building blocks of proteins are organic chemical compounds.

clue.text: Go very quietly round end of lane

indicators.note: round means the musical letters go around the other piece

parts.note: PP is pianissimo, the musical direction for very quietly

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of lane is used

explanation.surface: Creep softly around the bottom of the lane.
explanation.walkthrough: PP, pianissimo, goes round E, the end of 'lane'.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go: energy and vigour.

clue.text: Seat that's amazing — not hard!

indicators.note: not means the letter for hard is taken away from the exclamation

parts.note: phew is an exclamation of amazement or relief
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A chair that's astonishing, but soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' removes H from PHEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A long bench in a church.

clue.text: Light touch from boy or girl

definitions.meaning: a gentle tap with the hand
a name used for either sex, short for Patrick or Patricia

explanation.surface: A gentle tap from a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle stroke with the palm, and a unisex short name for Patrick or Patricia.

clue.text: Peter's nine mates stupidly getting drunk?

indicators.note: stupidly means the letters of the words before it are arranged in a foolish new order

explanation.surface: Peter and his nine friends behave foolishly while drinking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges PETERSNINEMATES; the question mark marks the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of restraint, especially excessive drinking of alcohol.

clue.text: Funny guy with little sex appeal

parts.note: W is the short, little, form of with; that the letters also sit at the front of with is a coincidence
it is a dated term for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A comedian who has hardly any allure.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal comes from the 1927 film It starring Clara Bow, the It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever, humorous person, a joker.

clue.text: Man sitting in tree — position for a lord

indicators.note: sitting in means the man goes inside the tree

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man perched in a tree, said to be fit for a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank or domain of a baron, a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Murderer, a male turning raving mad

indicators.note: turning means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A killer and a man going wildly insane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses CAINAM to give the answer; 'Murderer' looks like the definition but supplies CAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word describes someone wildly frenzied.

clue.text: Cunning journalist, not straight

parts.note: arch means sly or cunning
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A sly reporter who is less than honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not straight' looks like dishonesty, fitting the sly journalist; it means curved.
explanation.definitionFit: Curved like a bow, bent rather than in a line.

clue.text: Distant line of houses generating litter

parts.note: far means distant
a row is a line of houses, a terrace

explanation.surface: A remote terrace that produces rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' suggests rubbish; it is a brood of piglets.
explanation.definitionFit: A brood of newborn piglets born to a sow at one time.

clue.text: Hardy Adam undone by snake

indicators.note: undone means the letters of the two names are unpicked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hardy Adam is brought down by a serpent, as in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undone' rearranges HARDYADAM; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the king cobra, as well as a tree nymph.

clue.text: Bathroom — note something useful there

parts.note: loo is informal for a lavatory or bathroom
fah is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: In the bathroom, a note on something handy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'Bathroom': 'there' refers back to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried gourd used as a scrubbing sponge in the bath.

clue.text: Confused in Irish fens, they complete the course

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the words that follow are muddled

explanation.surface: Bewildered in the Irish marshes, some runners still make it to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges IRISHFENS; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who complete a race are the ones who reach the end of it.

clue.text: Full of passion a brief time, then 'orrendous

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
the dropped h mimics Cockney speech, so 'orrendous suggests horrid without its h

explanation.surface: An intense moment followed by something dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orrendous signals a dropped H, as in Cockney: horrendous is horrid, and without H it gives ORRID.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid describes something burning hot, hence passionate and intense.

clue.text: Overwhelmingly powerful places in Ireland

parts.note: Knock is a shrine village in County Mayo
Down is a county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Locations in Ireland noted for overwhelming force.
explanation.walkthrough: Knock is a Marian shrine village in Mayo; Down is a Northern Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockdown blow is one strong enough to floor someone.
